parts.text: Some students are investigating the resistance of a power supply. They are using the circuit shown in Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) A student connects the crocodile clip to the resistance wire at positions which give particular values of the potential difference V between terminals P and Q . He measures the current I in the circuit for each position. On Fig. 2.1, draw a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference V between terminals P and Q . [1]

ms.label: 2(a)(i)
ms.text: correct voltmeter symbol connected in parallel across P and Q

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Fig. 2.2 shows the ammeter reading for a value of V = 2.2 V. Read, and record in Table 2.1, this value of I . Table 2.1 I / A V / V 2.2 0.47 2.0 0.55 1.8 0.69 1.6 0.76 1.4 [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of V / V ( y -axis) against I / A ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 2(b)
ms.text:
graph:
axes labelled with quantity and unit
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
plots all correct to ½ small square
well-judged straight line and thin line, precise plots

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Determine the gradient M of the line you have drawn. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. M = .......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(c)(i)
ms.text: M present and triangle method seen on graph

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The gradient M is numerically equal to the resistance R of the power supply. Write down the resistance R to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. R = .......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 2(c)(ii)
ms.text:
R in range 1.8 to 2.4 Ω
2 or 3 sig figs and unit = Ω

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
suitable reason:
wire becomes too hot,
current exceeds full scale deflection(owtte) of meter / becomes too large

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) In this type of experiment, it is possible to change the potential difference by using a variable resistor rather than using different lengths of a resistance wire. In the space below, draw the standard circuit symbol for a variable resistor. [1]

ms.label: 2(e)
ms.text:
correct symbol for variable resistor
(rectangle with strike-through arrow only)
